chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: The Harry Rosenthal pseudonym session, Chick Bullock and Ray Jessup
summary: Kline and Hutto discuss records issued under pseudonyms, Chick Bullock's hundreds of sides and Jessup's Melody Makers backing, with Morehouse admiring the other players.

bands.name: Ray Jessup and His Melody Makers

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who is Harry Rosenthal and his orchestra?
Yes. You made some records, Harry Rosenthal and his orchestra including Benny Goodman, Toots Mondello, Arthur Rollini, George Van Epps, Harry Goodman, Sammy Weiss, 1934. Do you remember that?
It was under the name of Harry Rosenthal which I suspect was Benny Goodman. Although I don't know. Does it mean anything to you Ed?
No, other than I know that a lot of Benny's records in thirty three and thirty four, they just put all sorts of pseudonyms on them.
The Bill Dodge orchestra and all of that. Goodman. We do have in the presentation I guess a Chick Bullock side with Chauncey.
Yes. He literally made hundreds and hundreds of records in the thirties.
Yeah and do you know Jerry Valburn the big Ellington man?
I have - I have some things that were made by other people, things that I can't do.
And I love them. Because then I can go into a place like this and sing out, you know.
So that made me a big man with him.
Uh huh. Was Ray Jessup one of those names they made up? No Ray Jessup really was. No, I'm sorry, trombone.
Ray Jessup and his Melody Makers backed Chick Bullock.
Then Jack Shilkret. Jack Shilkret's orchestra?
